Before a model can be trained, before a feature vector can be computed, before
making any prediction — data must move. It must be collected, cleaned,
transformed, validated, and delivered reliably. **Data engineering is that
discipline.**

If you look at the field of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science today,
everyone talks about the glamorous side: training Large Language Models,
running neural networks, and building autonomous agents. But here is the
industry's open secret: **an AI model is only as smart as the data you feed
it.** Without data engineers building the invisible roads, pipes, and
purification systems, data remains trapped, messy, and useless.

This course gives you a complete mental model of modern data engineering for
AI systems — how pipelines are designed, where they break, what patterns
experienced engineers use to make them reliable, and how the data layer
connects to every other part of the ML system.

## Modern Data Architectures — Day 1

Today we explore the **Modern Data Engineering Ecosystem** — the foundational
infrastructure that powers all contemporary AI and analytical systems. We'll
look at how data engineering evolved from legacy on-premise systems into
highly scalable, cloud-native pipelines built specifically to feed downstream
AI and business-intelligence workloads.

Subtopics for today:

1. Evolution of Data Architectures — from Data Warehouses to Lakehouses
2. Core building blocks — decoupling compute and storage
3. Data integration paradigms — ETL vs. ELT
4. Delta Lake and ACID transactions
5. **Hands-on lab:** building a mini-lakehouse using Delta Lake

the [lab notebook](Day1_Lab.ipynb).
